<reason>B made the stronger net-benefit comparison: English connects non-anglophone communities to one another, while A did not establish that translation could preserve equivalent access at comparable cost. A identified credible participation and prestige harms, but insufficiently defended its leap from those harms to predominant, irreversible cultural loss. B directly answered the pressure questions and explained how local-language support could coexist with the shared network. A weakened its case by alleging unanswered questions before B’s scheduled response and overstating B’s concessions.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B turned A’s epistemic-flattening concern against its translation alternative: preserving local meanings still requires expert judgment, and translating documents does not automatically reproduce direct collaboration. This materially undermined A’s decisive claim that the benefits were readily portable while the harms were not.</best_rebuttal>
